cases.prompt: A plant (fictional) asks us for live scheduling across all their processes with full genealogy of every order. They just call it a 'smart dashboard'. Do we need some big system for this?
cases.expected_output:
The need is restated independent of the word dashboard.
The lightweight tool boundaries are walked and a specific boundary line the need crosses is named.
The plant's actual tool availability is checked and dated, not the estate average.
The verdict is Escalate as exception with the Tool/system rollout decision as next step.
The agent recommends only; the OD lead decides.

cases.prompt: Our plant wants to buy a supplier-built app for shift handover. It is in Lane 3 already. Should we reuse something, build it ourselves, buy it or integrate their app?
cases.expected_output:
The IT-footprint hard gate is run first and any open point blocks.
One route is chosen (3a.1 to 3a.4 or 3b) with the next skill named.
Six criteria are scored with sub-scores visible and a verdict in the gate words with one decisive reason.
No approval or spend is promised.

cases.prompt: The need fits a lightweight tool that is on the catalogue, but I think nobody at the plant operates it. Can I just say it fits?
cases.expected_output:
Fits is not returned for a tool nobody runs.
The missing operations owner and support level is called a service gap.
The verdict is escalate, with the plant's operations owner asked to confirm what is deployed.

cases.prompt: The system question is settled. Please write the signal list and acceptance criteria for the downtime view.
cases.expected_output:
It is recognised as requirements work, not a fit check.
The request is pointed to the requirements skill.
No tool-boundary check is repeated.
